name: Sashiko
note: Japanese running-stitch reinforcement and decorative pattern traditions, often using white stitches on indigo cloth with geometric repeats.

name: Boro
note: Japanese mending and patchwork traditions associated with layered cloth repair, visible running stitch, reuse, and time-worn surface history.

name: Kantha
note: South Asian running-stitch quilting and embroidery traditions where dense stitched lines create texture, narrative figures, and rippling fields.

name: Chikankari
note: Fine whitework embroidery tradition associated with Lucknow, using delicate shadow, floral, and surface stitches on lightweight cloth.

name: Phulkari
note: Punjabi embroidery tradition known for bright silk floss, geometric floral fields, and dense surface coverage on cloth.

name: Suzani
note: Central Asian embroidered textiles featuring bold medallions, vines, flowers, suns, and large-scale domestic/ceremonial compositions.

name: Palestinian Tatreez
note: Counted cross-stitch tradition using regional motifs, geometric patterns, and garment-based storytelling. Treat as living cultural heritage, not generic decoration.

name: Mexican Otomi Inspired Motif Logic
note: Otomi embroidery is associated with vibrant animals, plants, and symmetrical folk compositions. Use respectfully; do not claim authenticity without source/context.

name: Ukrainian Vyshyvanka
note: Ukrainian embroidered garment traditions with regional geometric, floral, and symbolic motifs, often worked in counted or surface stitches.

name: Hungarian Kalocsa
note: Hungarian floral embroidery tradition known for colorful flowers and bold satin-style floral ornament.

name: Norwegian Hardanger
note: Norwegian counted whitework with satin blocks, cutwork openings, woven bars, and precise geometric structure.

name: Brazilian Dimensional Embroidery
note: Raised floral embroidery using rayon threads and dimensional stitches like bullion, cast-on, drizzle, and woven forms.

name: Jacobean Crewel
note: Historic English crewelwork style with scrolling vines, fantasy flowers, animals, and wool thread.

name: Mountmellick Whitework
note: Irish whitework tradition using matte cotton thread, raised stitches, and botanical motifs on cotton sateen.

name: Aari Embroidery
note: Hook-based embroidery used in South Asian decorative work and couture embellishment, related to tambour-style chain creation.

name: Zardozi
note: Metal-thread and embellishment embroidery tradition associated with South Asian luxury textiles, using metallic threads, beads, sequins, and couching.
